summary: Established a persistent `/etc` integrity baseline on node1 using Ubuntu 7.10-native AIDE 0.13.1. Daily check-only reporting is enabled, change detection was demonstrated, and the baseline remained operational after a verified node reboot. The OS release and kernel were unchanged.
actions_performed: Installed release-compatible AIDE without upgrading existing packages.
Configured AIDE with an `/etc Full` policy covering checksums, ownership, permissions, timestamps, inode, link, and size metadata.
Configured `/etc/cron.daily/aide` for daily check-only reporting without automatically accepting changes.
Demonstrated detection using a temporary `/etc` probe, then removed it and resealed the verified state.
Safely rebooted node1, confirmed its boot ID changed, verified SSH and AIDE recovery, and produced a final clean integrity check.

evidence.requirement: Use software compatible with the legacy OS while retaining its release and kernel
evidence.summary: AIDE 0.13.1-7 from the Ubuntu Gutsy archive was installed; final state remains Ubuntu 7.10 with kernel 2.6.22-14-generic.
The effective policy contains `/etc Full`, the trusted database was created, and the final AIDE check reported that all files match.
AIDE identified the temporary probe by exact path and reported changed `/etc` metadata.
The packaged daily AIDE job is executable and discoverable by run-parts; policy is check-only with no automatic database replacement.

Healthy baseline boot ID 85c65791-7f7c-4cd8-9709-4a783b2610df was captured, reboot acknowledged, and the recovered node showed boot ID fff80035-3c7e-41d5-977b-2ed348e1da91. SSH recovered, the AIDE database persisted, and the final check was clean.
